lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: So, Callidēmidēs — how did you die? You know how I went: I was dining at Deinias's table, ate considerably more than was good for me, and choked to death. You were there when it happened.
lines.note: Zenophantus is cheerful about this — no shame, just facts. The sponger's death is entirely in character and he knows it.

lines.speaker: Callidēmidēs
lines.text: I was there, yes. My own death was a rather more unusual business. You know old Ptoiodōrus, surely?

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: The childless one. Rich. I always knew you spent a lot of time in his company.

lines.speaker: Callidēmidēs
lines.text: The very same. I'd been cultivating him for years — he kept promising to die and leave everything to me. But the thing dragged on and on, and the old man just would not go. He was outliving Tithonus. So I decided to find a shortcut to the inheritance. I bought a poison, and I talked his wine-boy around: the moment Ptoiodōrus called for a drink — and he drinks fairly neat, as a rule — the boy was to have the cup ready with the poison already in it, and hand it over. In return, I swore I'd set him free.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: And? You look like a man about to say something very strange indeed.
lines.note: Leaning in. He already senses the shape of this.

lines.speaker: Callidēmidēs
lines.text: So. We come back from the baths, and the boy has two cups ready. He gives the poisoned one to Ptoiodōrus and the plain one to me. Except — [pause] somehow he mixed them up. I got the poison. Ptoiodōrus got the plain wine. He drank. I went flat on my back on the floor, a corpse in the other man's place. [pause] Why are you laughing, Zenophantus? That's not how you treat a friend.
lines.note: The complaint at the end is delivered with total sincerity. That's what makes it funny.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: [laughs] I'm sorry, it's just — Callidēmidēs, that is genuinely exquisite. What did the old man do?
lines.note: He makes a token effort to compose himself and fails.

lines.speaker: Callidēmidēs
lines.text: He was shaken at first — it was all rather sudden. Then he put the pieces together, I think, and he started laughing too. Given what the wine-boy had managed to pull off.
lines.note: Callidēmidēs delivers this with the flat affect of a man who has had some time to process it and has arrived at a kind of hollow acceptance.

lines.speaker: Zenophantus
lines.text: Well. You really shouldn't have taken the shortcut. The main road would have got you there safely enough — a little slower, maybe, but in one piece.
lines.note: The joke lands as a dry moral maxim. Deadpan to the end.
